questions.q: What is the very first step in designing Alderney Health Systems' hybrid architecture, before any infrastructure decisions?
options: Choosing which cloud provider offers the cheapest compute
Provisioning the AKS burst-compute cluster
Classifying the data into regulated/immovable versus de-identified/portable categories
Writing the Terraform module for the network
questions.explain: Data classification is a compliance decision that has to happen first -- the rest of the architecture exists to enforce that split, not to decide it.

questions.q: How does Alderney's conditional access policy treat on-prem claims database access versus cloud burst-compute access?
options: Access is governed by the same identity and the same conditional access policy on both sides, with no separate weaker rule for the cloud
The cloud side uses a looser policy since it never touches identifiable data
On-prem access requires no authentication at all
Each environment uses a completely separate, unrelated identity provider
questions.explain: One conditional access policy spans both the on-prem database and the cloud burst-compute resources, enforced identically on either side.

questions.q: Why does the de-identified extract's storage account have public network access disabled, reachable only through a private endpoint?
options: Because Azure requires this setting on every storage account by default
To reduce storage costs
Because private endpoints are faster than public endpoints for all workloads
To make it structurally impossible for raw claims data to reach the cloud, rather than relying only on a written policy
questions.explain: Disabling public access and exposing only a private endpoint over the ExpressRoute path enforces the data-residency boundary at the network layer itself.

questions.q: What does the cloud-side AKS burst-compute job in this lab ever read from or write to?
options: The on-prem claims database directly, over the public internet
Only the de-identified extract storage account, never the raw on-prem database
A randomly selected subset of the full PHI dataset
Nothing -- it only processes synthetic test data
questions.explain: The burst job only ever touches the de-identified extract that already crossed the compliance boundary -- nothing identifiable has a path to reach it.

questions.q: What makes a hybrid architecture design actually verifiable by a compliance reviewer, according to this lesson?
options: A 40-page Terraform configuration with no accompanying explanation
A verbal assurance from the engineering team that the design is compliant

A one-page summary a non-architect reviewer can check against the regulatory rule, covering what data crosses the boundary, what enforces that, who can access either side, and where regulated data never moves from
The absence of any written documentation, so nothing can be audited incorrectly
questions.explain: A design that can't be explained in a few plain sentences to a non-engineer reviewer usually isn't actually enforceable, regardless of how clean the underlying code is.
